```{r}

# 1. Load the original data
train_raw <- read.csv("data/data-train.csv")
test_raw  <- read.csv("data/data-test.csv")

train <- train_raw
test  <- test_raw

predictors <- c("St", "Re", "Fr")
raw_moments <- paste0("R_moment_", 1:4)
```

```{r}

# 2. Check required columns
stopifnot(
  all(c(predictors, raw_moments) %in% names(train)),
  all(predictors %in% names(test))
)

# Check that the required columns are numeric and have no missing values.
# Fr = Inf is an intentional simulation setting, not a missing value.
stopifnot(
  all(vapply(train[c(predictors, raw_moments)], is.numeric, logical(1))),
  all(vapply(test[predictors], is.numeric, logical(1))),
  !anyNA(train[c(predictors, raw_moments)]),
  !anyNA(test[predictors])
)

# Re, St, and the raw moments must be finite.
stopifnot(
  all(is.finite(as.matrix(train[c("St", "Re", raw_moments)]))),
  all(is.finite(as.matrix(test[c("St", "Re")]))),
  all(train$Fr > 0),
  all(test$Fr > 0)
)
```

```{r}

# 3. Convert raw moments into distribution summaries
m1 <- train$R_moment_1
m2 <- train$R_moment_2
m3 <- train$R_moment_3
m4 <- train$R_moment_4

train$mean_volume <- m1
train$variance_volume <- m2 - m1^2

# Stop and investigate if any variance is nonpositive.
if (any(train$variance_volume <= 0)) {
  stop("At least one calculated variance is nonpositive. Inspect those rows.")
}

train$sd_volume <- sqrt(train$variance_volume)

central_moment_3 <- m3 - 3 * m1 * m2 + 2 * m1^3
central_moment_4 <- m4 - 4 * m1 * m3 + 6 * m1^2 * m2 - 3 * m1^4

train$skewness_volume <- central_moment_3 / train$sd_volume^3
train$kurtosis_volume <- central_moment_4 / train$sd_volume^4

response_names <- c(
  "mean_volume", "variance_volume", "sd_volume",
  "skewness_volume", "kurtosis_volume"
)

stopifnot(
  all(is.finite(as.matrix(train[response_names])))
)
```

```{r}
#| message: false

# 4. Print a compact preparation check
preparation_check <- data.frame(
  dataset = c("Training", "Test"),
  rows = c(nrow(train_raw), nrow(test_raw)),
  original_columns = c(ncol(train_raw), ncol(test_raw)),
  missing_entries = c(sum(is.na(train_raw)), sum(is.na(test_raw))),
  duplicate_input_settings = c(
    sum(duplicated(train_raw[predictors])),
    sum(duplicated(test_raw[predictors]))
  ),
  infinite_Fr_settings = c(
    sum(is.infinite(train_raw$Fr)),
    sum(is.infinite(test_raw$Fr))
  )
)

knitr::kable(preparation_check, caption = "Data preparation checks")

# Preview the predictors and calculated responses
knitr::kable(
  head(train[c(predictors, response_names)]),
  digits = 5,
  caption = "First six training observations"
)

# Summarize the calculated responses
summary(train[response_names])
```

```{r}

#| label: predictor-setup
#| message: false

library(ggplot2)

# Check that all test predictor levels occur in the training data
stopifnot(
  all(test$Re %in% train$Re),
  all(test$Fr %in% train$Fr),
  all(test$St %in% train$St)
)

# Use identical factor levels in training and test data
Re_levels <- sort(unique(train$Re))
Fr_levels <- sort(unique(train$Fr))
St_levels <- sort(unique(train$St))

train$Re_factor <- factor(train$Re, levels = Re_levels)
test$Re_factor  <- factor(test$Re, levels = Re_levels)

train$Fr_factor <- factor(train$Fr, levels = Fr_levels)
test$Fr_factor  <- factor(test$Fr, levels = Fr_levels)

# Inverse Froude number: Inf becomes 0
train$inv_Fr <- 1 / train$Fr
test$inv_Fr  <- 1 / test$Fr

# Compact summary of the original predictors
predictor_summary <- data.frame(
  Predictor = c("Re", "Fr", "St"),
  Training_levels = sapply(train[predictors], function(x) length(unique(x))),
  Test_levels = sapply(test[predictors], function(x) length(unique(x))),
  Training_min = sapply(train[predictors], min),
  Training_max = sapply(train[predictors], max),
  row.names = NULL
)

# Explicitly match the displayed predictor order
predictor_summary <- data.frame(
  Predictor = predictors,
  Training_levels = sapply(train[predictors], function(x) length(unique(x))),
  Test_levels = sapply(test[predictors], function(x) length(unique(x))),
  Training_min = sapply(train[predictors], min),
  Training_max = sapply(train[predictors], max),
  row.names = NULL
)

knitr::kable(
  predictor_summary,
  caption = "Predictor ranges and number of distinct settings"
)

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(Fr = Fr_levels, Inverse_Fr = 1 / Fr_levels),
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Froude number and its reciprocal"
)
```

```{r}

#| label: predictor-counts
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.5

# Combine predictors only; no response values are used here
design_data <- rbind(
  data.frame(train[predictors], Dataset = "Training"),
  data.frame(test[predictors], Dataset = "Test")
)

design_data$Dataset <- factor(
  design_data$Dataset,
  levels = c("Training", "Test")
)

# Helper function for count plots
plot_setting_counts <- function(variable, setting_levels, axis_label) {

  plot_data <- data.frame(
    Setting = factor(design_data[[variable]], levels = setting_levels),
    Dataset = design_data$Dataset
  )

  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Setting, fill = Dataset)) +
    geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Training" = "#2166AC", "Test" = "#D6604D")) +
    labs(
      x = axis_label,
      y = "Number of simulations",
      fill = "Dataset"
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
}

plot_setting_counts("Re", Re_levels, "Reynolds number (Re)")
plot_setting_counts("Fr", Fr_levels, "Froude number (Fr)")
plot_setting_counts("St", St_levels, "Stokes number (St)")

```

```{r}

#| label: simulation-counts

# Include every combination, even combinations with no observations
design_counts <- expand.grid(
  Re = Re_levels,
  Fr = Fr_levels
)

design_counts <- design_counts[
  order(design_counts$Re, design_counts$Fr),
]

design_counts$Training <- mapply(
  function(re, fr) sum(train$Re == re & train$Fr == fr),
  design_counts$Re,
  design_counts$Fr
)

design_counts$Test <- mapply(
  function(re, fr) sum(test$Re == re & test$Fr == fr),
  design_counts$Re,
  design_counts$Fr
)

design_counts$Total <- design_counts$Training + design_counts$Test

knitr::kable(
  design_counts,
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Simulation counts within each Re and Fr combination"
)

# Check for exact input settings shared by training and test data
shared_settings <- merge(
  unique(train[predictors]),
  unique(test[predictors]),
  by = predictors
)

cat(
  "\nNumber of exact input settings shared by training and test:",
  nrow(shared_settings),
  "\n"
)
```

```{r}

#| label: response-plotting-data

response_columns <- c(
  "mean_volume",
  "sd_volume",
  "skewness_volume",
  "kurtosis_volume"
)

response_labels <- c(
  "Mean",
  "Standard deviation",
  "Skewness",
  "Kurtosis"
)

# Confirm that the responses exist and are finite
stopifnot(
  all(response_columns %in% names(train)),
  all(is.finite(as.matrix(train[response_columns])))
)

# One row per simulation and response
response_long <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(seq_along(response_columns), function(j) {
    data.frame(
      St = train$St,
      Re_factor = train$Re_factor,
      Fr_factor = train$Fr_factor,
      Response = response_labels[j],
      Value = train[[response_columns[j]]]
    )
  })
)

response_long$Response <- factor(
  response_long$Response,
  levels = response_labels
)

# The log-scale plots below require positive values.
# Stop rather than silently removing nonpositive observations.
stopifnot(all(response_long$Value > 0))

# Consistent colors for Reynolds-number settings
Re_colors <- c(
  "90" = "#2166AC",
  "224" = "#1B7837",
  "398" = "#B2182B"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: candidate-transformations

# Check domains before taking logarithms
stopifnot(
  all(train$St > 0), all(test$St > 0),
  all(train$Re > 0), all(test$Re > 0),
  all(as.matrix(train[response_columns]) > 0)
)

# Candidate predictor transformations
train$log10_St <- log10(train$St)
test$log10_St  <- log10(test$St)

train$log10_Re <- log10(train$Re)
test$log10_Re  <- log10(test$Re)

# Candidate response transformations: training data only
for (response in response_columns) {
  train[[paste0("log10_", response)]] <- log10(train[[response]])
}

# Predictor transformation reference
transformation_reference <- data.frame(
  Predictor = c("St", "Re", "Fr"),
  Candidate = c("log10(St)", "log10(Re)", "1/Fr"),
  Purpose = c(
    "Represent proportional changes in particle inertia",
    "Represent proportional changes in Reynolds number",
    "Represent relative gravity strength; Inf becomes zero"
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  transformation_reference,
  caption = "Candidate predictor transformations"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: matched-gravity-contrasts

#| fig-height: 6

matching_columns <- c("St", "Re_factor", "Response", "Value")

strong_gravity <- response_long[
  response_long$Fr_factor == "0.052",
  matching_columns
]

no_gravity <- response_long[
  response_long$Fr_factor == "Inf",
  matching_columns
]

# Match on all remaining predictors and the response being compared
gravity_contrasts <- merge(
  strong_gravity,
  no_gravity,
  by = c("St", "Re_factor", "Response"),
  suffixes = c("_strong", "_none")
)

gravity_contrasts$log10_ratio <- log10(
  gravity_contrasts$Value_strong /
    gravity_contrasts$Value_none
)

# Show how many matched settings support each Re comparison
matched_counts <- unique(
  gravity_contrasts[c("Re_factor", "St")]
)

knitr::kable(
  as.data.frame(table(Re = matched_counts$Re_factor)),
  caption = "Number of matched St settings for the gravity comparison"
)

ggplot(
  gravity_contrasts,
  aes(
    x = St,
    y = log10_ratio,
    color = Re_factor,
    group = Re_factor
  )
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "grey50"
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = Re_colors) +
  scale_x_log10(

  facet_wrap(~ Response, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +

    title = "Gravity contrasts at matched predictor settings",

    y = "log10(strong-gravity response / no-gravity response)",
```

```{r}

#| label: create-validation-folds

# Reproducible random assignment
set.seed(325)

K <- 5L

# Stable identifiers matching the current training-data row order
train$row_id <- seq_len(nrow(train))

# Identify the observed simulation regimes
train$regime <- interaction(
  train$Re_factor,
  train$Fr_factor,
  drop = TRUE,
  sep = " / "
)

train$cv_fold <- NA_integer_

# Randomize the labels of the five folds
fold_order <- sample(seq_len(K))

# Cycle through fold labels across regimes.
# This keeps total fold sizes and within-regime counts balanced.
offset <- 0L

for (regime_name in levels(train$regime)) {

  rows <- which(train$regime == regime_name)

  assignments <- fold_order[
    ((seq_along(rows) - 1L + offset) %% K) + 1L
  ]

  # Randomly assign these fold labels to observations in this regime
  train$cv_fold[rows] <- assignments[
    sample.int(length(rows))
  ]

  offset <- offset + length(rows)
}

# Save row indices for each training/validation split
cv_folds <- lapply(seq_len(K), function(k) {
  list(
    analysis = which(train$cv_fold != k),
    assessment = which(train$cv_fold == k)
  )
})

names(cv_folds) <- paste0("Fold_", seq_len(K))
```

```{r}

#| label: check-validation-folds

# Every row must have a valid fold assignment
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(train$cv_fold),
  all(train$cv_fold %in% seq_len(K))
)

# Every observation must appear in exactly one assessment set
assessment_rows <- unlist(
  lapply(cv_folds, function(x) x$assessment),
  use.names = FALSE
)

stopifnot(
  identical(sort(assessment_rows), seq_len(nrow(train)))
)

# Check separation and regime coverage in every split
for (k in seq_len(K)) {

  analysis_rows <- cv_folds[[k]]$analysis
  assessment_rows <- cv_folds[[k]]$assessment

  stopifnot(
    length(intersect(analysis_rows, assessment_rows)) == 0L,
    length(analysis_rows) + length(assessment_rows) == nrow(train),
    all(
      levels(train$regime) %in%
        as.character(train$regime[analysis_rows])
    ),
    all(
      levels(train$regime) %in%
        as.character(train$regime[assessment_rows])
    )
  )
}

# Overall fold sizes
fold_summary <- data.frame(
  Fold = seq_len(K),
  Training_rows = vapply(
    cv_folds,
    function(x) length(x$analysis),
    integer(1)
  ),
  Validation_rows = vapply(
    cv_folds,
    function(x) length(x$assessment),
    integer(1)
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  fold_summary,
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Training and validation sample sizes"
)

# Counts of held-out observations by regime and fold
regime_fold_counts <- table(
  Regime = train$regime,
  Fold = factor(train$cv_fold, levels = seq_len(K))
)

regime_fold_table <- data.frame(
  Regime = rownames(regime_fold_counts),
  as.data.frame.matrix(regime_fold_counts),
  row.names = NULL,
  check.names = FALSE
)

names(regime_fold_table)[-1] <- paste0("Fold ", seq_len(K))

knitr::kable(
  regime_fold_table,
  caption = "Validation observations from each Re / Fr regime"
)
```

```{r}
knitr::kable(
  small_St_counts,
  caption = "Validation observations with St at or below 0.3"
)
```

```{r}

#| label: validation-scoring-functions

# Responses to evaluate separately
cv_responses <- c(
  "mean_volume",
  "sd_volume",
  "skewness_volume",
  "kurtosis_volume"
)

# Score original-scale observed values and held-out predictions
score_predictions <- function(observed, predicted) {

  stopifnot(
    is.numeric(observed),
    is.numeric(predicted),
    length(observed) == length(predicted),
    length(observed) > 0L,
    all(is.finite(observed)),
    all(is.finite(predicted))
  )

  errors <- observed - predicted

  data.frame(
    RMSE = sqrt(mean(errors^2)),
    MAE = mean(abs(errors)),
    Nonpositive_predictions = sum(predicted <= 0)
  )
}

# Retain the validation settings for later modeling steps
cv_settings <- list(
  seed = 325L,
  folds = K,
  responses = cv_responses,
  primary_metric = "Original-scale RMSE",
  secondary_metric = "Original-scale MAE"
)

cat(
  "Validation setup complete:",
  K, "folds;",
  length(cv_responses), "responses;",
  "primary metric =", cv_settings$primary_metric,
  "\n"
)
```
